rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
rules.description: Leaking information about an exception, such as messages and stack traces, to an external user can expose implementation details that are useful to an attacker for developing a subsequent exploit.

rules.cwe_name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Validation
rules.description: A Unicode transformation is using a remote user-controlled data. The transformation is a Unicode normalization using the algorithms "NFC" or "NFKC". rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: Use of a non-constant-time verification routine to check the value of an secret, possibly allowing a timing attack to retrieve sensitive information.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: Data provided remotely is used in this external API without sanitization, which could be a security risk.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
rules.description: Building log entries from user-controlled data is vulnerable to insertion of forged log entries by a malicious user.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Binding a socket to all interfaces opens it up to traffic from any IPv4 address and is therefore associated with security risks.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Logging sensitive information without encryption or hashing can expose it to an attacker.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A string formatting operation, such as '"%s: %s, %s" % (a,b)', where the number of conversion specifiers in the format string differs from the number of values to be formatted will raise a TypeError.
